examples.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =2.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & 8 & -6 \\ -15 & 14 & -9 \\ -5 & 4 & -1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-10 & 8 & -6 \\ -15 & 12 & -9 \\ -5 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-10{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}-6{x}_{3}=0 \\ -15{x}_{1}+12{x}_{2}-9{x}_{3}=0 \\ -5{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-10 & 8 & -6 & 0 \\ -15 & 12 & -9 & 0 \\ -5 & 4 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & 3 & 0 \\ -15 & 12 & -9 & 0 \\ -5 & 4 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Which of the following is a basis of the eigenspace corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =5.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 5\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=0.$ 

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the required basis is 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}.
$$
